text: Praeterea Syrorum Damascenorum (qui Adarezero Sophenae regi subsidio venerant) viginti duo millia occidit:
note: *Damascēnōrum* capital, an adjective of a people, as the next verse's *Syriæ Damascēnōrum* and the settled *Isrāēlītic-* (1738 *damascenorum*) (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: Postquam intellexit Thois Hemathae rex, Adarezeri vires omnes a Davide fractas,
note: paragraph: Toi's embassy; 8:1–14 was 276 words in one (decision 52), and here the BSB breaks (b m) and *Postquam* begins a sentence after 8:8's *vāsa. H.* (1738 runs on from 8:1 to 8:18) (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: Ac postquam venit ille Mephibosethus, Jonathanis filius, Sauli nepos, et Davidi ad pedes suppliciter accidit, David eum sic adlocutus est: “Mephibosethe.” Cui ille: “Ecce me tuum.”
note: paragraph: Mephibosheth before David; 1738 indents here (text/orig/2SA.usfm) and *Ac postquam* begins a sentence; David's call and Mephibosheth's answer direct (*Mephībōsethe*, *ecce mē tuum*), after 1738's colons, which stay (no *inquit*, as r2's 4:8); capital at each speech's start (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: Et David, “Bono es animo,” inquit, “nam ego te beneficiis adficiam, propter Jonathanem patrem tuum, tibique omnes agros Sauli avi tui reddam, faciamque, ut ad mensam meam semper cibum capias.”
note: David's words direct (*ego tē … afficiam*); *X: words, inquit*: the colon after *Dāvīd* a comma, *inquit* set off by commas and the quotation closed and reopened (decision 65, 1 Sam 1:17); capital at the speech's start (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: Atque ille supplex, “Quis ego sum,” inquit, “ut tu me, mortuo cane viliorem, respicias?”
note: Mephibosheth's answer direct; the colon after *supplex* a comma before *inquit* (as 9:7, 1 Sam 1:17) (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: Tum David vocato Sibae Sauli famulo dicit: “Quidquid Saulus ejusque tota domus habuit, id domini tui filio do.
note: David's words to Ziba direct, 9:9–10 (*dō*, *Tū eī terram colēs*), after 1738's colon; capital at the speech's start (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: Tu ei terram coles cum tuis filiis atque servis, proventumque vehes, quo victu utatur ipse. Nam Mephibosethus quidem, domini tui filius, mihi perpetuo convictor erit.” Habebat autem Siba filios quindecim, et servos viginti.
note: David's speech closes at *erit* (*mihi … convīctor*), the narrator's note on Ziba's household outside it, as the BSB (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: Itaque regi respondit, facturum se, quidquid ille jussisset. “Ergo cibum capiet ad mensam meam Mephibosethus,” inquit ille, “sicut unus de filiis regiis.”
note: Ziba's answer reported (*factūrum sē*), unmarked where the BSB quotes; the king's words direct (*ad mēnsam meam*; the KJV's "said the king"), the parenthesis *(inquit ille)* made commas and the quotation closed and reopened (decision 65, 1 Sam 1:22) (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: Tum Ammonitae, intelligentes, Davidem sibi infensum esse, mercede arcessiverunt Syrorum Bethrohobanorum, et Syrorum Sophenorum, viginti millia peditum, regemque Maacham cum mille, et Istobum cum duodecim millibus hominum.
note: paragraph: the Ammonites hire the Arameans; 1738 indents here and the BSB breaks (b m); *Bethrohōbānōrum*, *Sophēnōrum* capital, adjectives of peoples (1738 lower case), as *Damascēnōrum* 8:5 (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: Joabus (quum Ammonitae progressi, aciem ante portam instruxissent, Syri autem Sopheni et Rohobani, et Istobus, et Maacha, seorsum in agris)
note: *Sophēnī*, *Rohōbānī* capital, adjectives of peoples (1738 lower case), as 10:6 (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: intelligens, sibi proelium et a fronte imminere, et a tergo, delectos ex omni Israelitarum robore adversum Syros ordinavit;
note: no paragraph: the draft's (the BSB's heading) falls inside Castellio's sentence begun at 10:8 (*Jōabus … intellegēns … ōrdināvit*), and 1738 has no indent; the paragraph moved to 10:6, where 1738 indents (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: “Si me Syri prement; tu mihi feres auxilium: sin te Ammonitae prement; ego veniam tibi subsidio.
note: Joab's charge to Abishai direct, 10:11–12 (*sī mē … ego veniam*), after 10:10's *cum hujusmodī præceptīs:*; capital at the speech's start (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: Praesta te fortem, et pro populo nostro, proque urbibus Dei nostri fortiter pugnemus; et Jova faciet, quod ei visum fuerit.”
note: Joab's speech closes here, as the BSB (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: Tum Syri videntes, se ab Israelitis victos esse, coiverunt,
note: paragraph: the Arameans muster again; 1738 indents here and the BSB breaks (b m) (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: arcessitique ab Adarezero Syri, qui trans flumen incolebant, adfuerunt cum suis copiis, eisque praefuit Sobachus dux exercitus Adarezeriani.
note: a full stop at the end, where 1738 prints none (text/orig/2SA.usfm *adarezeriani* then 10:17 *Quod*, capital): the preview had made 10:17 *quod*; *Adarezeriānī* capital, an adjective from a name, as 1738's own *Adarezeriānōrum* 8:7 (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: caesis eorum septingentis quadrigariis, et quadraginta millibus equitum, occisoque ibi Sobacho, Adarezeriani exercitus duce.
note: *Adarezeriānī* capital, as 10:16 and 8:7 (1738 lower case here) (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: Tum David Joabo significavit, ut sibi Uriam Hettaeum mitteret.
note: paragraph: David sends for Uriah; 1738 indents here and the BSB breaks (b m); *Tum* begins a sentence after 11:5's full stop; 11:1–13 was 278 words in one (decision 52) (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: Cui Urias respondit: “Arca et Israelitae, et Judaei in umbraculis manent, et dominus meus Joabus, dominique mei milites sub dio castra habent: et ego domum meam ibo ad epulandum et potandum, et ad cubandum cum mea conjuge? At ita tibi vitam felicem precor, ut istud non faciam.”
note: Uriah's answer direct (*dominus meus*, *ego … ībō*, *nōn faciam*), after 1738's colon with *respondit*, no *inquit*, so the colon stays; capital at the speech's start (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: a quo enim occisum esse Abimelechum Jerobosethi filium? nonne dejecto in eum a femina de muro molae fragmine, apud Thebem interfectum fuisse? cur muris successissent? ut, inquam, responderet: “Etiam tuus Urias Hettaeus oppetiit.”
note: the king's angry questions (11:20–21) stay reported (*an nescīrent*, *occīsum esse*, *cūr … successissent*), unmarked where the BSB quotes them, with 1738's lower case inside the period; only the answer Joab gives the messenger is direct (*tuus Ūrīās*, addressed to David), after *respondēret:* (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: “Quum illi, nobis viribus superiores, in agros processissent, et nos eis ad portam usque institissemus;
note: the messenger's report direct, 11:23–24 (*nōbīs*, *nōs*, *in tuōs*, *tuus Ūrīās*), after 11:22's *atque ita retulit:*; capital at the speech's start (reader r3, 2026-11-21)

text: sagittarii jecerunt in tuos tela de muris, mortuique sunt de regiis quum alii, tum tuus Urias Hettaeus.”
note: the messenger's speech closes here; David's answer 11:25 is reported (*ut Jōabō nūntiāret, nē … ferret*), unmarked where the BSB quotes (reader r3, 2026-11-21)
